newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-THREE TOP 100 PLAYERS TO MISS FRENCH OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-THREE TOP 100 PLAYERS TO MISS FRENCH OPEN.

text.p: Only three players ranked in the world's top 100, including retired Swede Stefan Edberg and injured Russian Andrei Chesnokov, will miss the French Open this year.
Also missing from the list for the May 26-June 8 tournament issued by the organisers on Wednesday is 96th-ranked Swiss Jakob Hlasek who has also retired.
Chesnokov suffered a multiple fracture to his lower right leg in Philadelphia in February. He is ranked 74.
Edberg, who won all the majors except the French title, is still ranked in the top 20 despite retiring at the end of last year.
The lowest ranked player to make it directly into the men's draw is Canadian Daniel Nestor, the world number 107.
Organisers said they would announce their eight wild cards at a later date. Another 16 players will emerge from the qualifying competition.
In the women's list, Germany's Meike Babel has been included at number 30.
Babel, who has not played since Wimbledon 1995 due to a shoulder injury, benefits from a protected world ranking of 29, which she shares with American Amy Frazier.
